title: Winston Churchill Addresses the Canadian Parliament: 'Some Chicken! Some Neck!' — 1941
summary: In December 1941, Winston Churchill addressed the Canadian Parliament in Ottawa, delivering his legendary defiance of Nazi invasion: 'Some chicken! Some neck!'
keywords: Historical Dialogue 148: சர்ச்சிலும் கனடா நாடாளுமன்றமும்: “என்ன கோழி! என்ன கழுத்து!” — 1941
full_text:
On December 30, 1941, amidst the darkest hours of the Second World War, British Prime Minister Winston Churchill rose to address a joint session of the Canadian Parliament in Ottawa.

Eighteen months earlier, following the tragic fall of France, French General Maxime Weygand had grimly predicted to his cabinet that Britain stood alone and doomed, stating: 'In three weeks, England will have her neck wrung like a chicken.'

Standing before the Canadian lawmakers, Churchill recounted the memory with dramatic pauses, his eyes flashing with defiance:
"When I warned them that Britain would fight on alone whatever they did, their generals told their Prime Minister and his dividing Cabinet: 'In three weeks England will have her neck wrung like a chicken!'"

Churchill paused. The silence in the chamber was electric. Then, thrusting his jaw forward with an unforgettable scowl that melted into a triumphant grin, he roared:
"Some chicken! Some neck!"

The entire parliament erupted into deafening laughter, cheers, and thundering ovations. Through three short words of supreme rhetorical wit, Churchill punctured fascist arrogance and galvanized Allied resolve across the globe.
